title: Catholics up early for Christmas Mass | Around The Web | wvnews.com
text:
Before they got to opening presents on Christmas Day, many residents got up with the sun to attend Mass at churches around the island.
For the majority of island residents who are of the Catholic faith, Christmas marks the celebration of the birth of Jesus Christ.
At the Dulce Nombre de Maria Cathedral-Basilica in Hagåtña, parishioners gathered at 6 a.m. to the smell of incense and the light of Christmas trees, to “nginge” the statue of the Niño Jesus, or the Christ Child.
A handful of other parishes held Misan Gayu or Simbang Gabi, the “‘rooster mass” as early as 4:30 a.m., though only St. Anthony Catholic Church in Tamuning hosted midnight mass.
At the Cathedral, parents John Duenas, 49, Tammy Iglesias, 44, of Toto, were in attendance at 6 a.m. with their six kids, all of them wearing matching “Family Christmas 2025” T-shirts.
After saying the morning prayers, the eight of them gathered out front of the Cathedral for a group photo in their shirts, which said, “Making Memories Together.”
Iglesias said they brought the kids to Mass with her parents in the morning, and planned to visit with Duenas’ parents afterwards.
Dad Duenas said the family goes to church on Christmas every year, and have been making matching shirts for the family for past four years.
“It’s just kind of fun,” Iglesias said of their tradition, adding that she had ordered this year’s batch of T-shirts as far out as July, so they would arrive in October.
“It’s a miracle they came in,” Duenas said.
“And they were the perfect size,” Iglesias added.
Mom said she was looking forward to the excitement of this Christmas, while Dad looked to, “peace, in life, and, you know, helping other people out a number of violence and stuff like that here in this island.”
Also in attendance at the Cathedral Thursday was Michael Santos, 29, of Dededo, who said he stopped in after getting off work early in the morning.
Santos said he wanted to get his Christmas Mass devotion done while the rest of the family was still sleeping, and looked forward to getting back home and opening presents.
“Happy for family, to be alive, and to be healthy,” he said.
Father William Mamangun, presiding over the Cathedral Mass Thursday morning, told parishioners to be patient with their loved ones and to remember Jesus this Christmas.
“As you celebrate Christmas today, and as you gather around people you love, family and friends, be reminded the imperfect, sinful people in front of you are the reason why Jesus became man,” Mamangun said in his homily.
“We need to be patient,” he said. “Jesus was born into this world not because we're perfect, but in spite of our imperfection, because of our sinfulness. And if we remember that on the days of our life, we will always be humble. We will never get discouraged when we see imperfections in other people.”
